senses.gloss:
√ṛj 'direct, stretch, attain'
present: [7.] ṛñjate (3p.) -- [6.] ṛñjáti ṛñjáte etc. -- [4.] ṛ́jyant ṛjyate -- ṛñjase (1s.) ṛñjasāná -- [1.] árjati 
perfect: ānarjus ānṝjús 
aorist: [3.] ārjijat -- ārjiṣṭa 
[future: arjiṣyati arjitā ]
verbal: ṛñjáse 
secondary: rjyate -- desiderative: arjijiṣa- -- causative: arjayati arjayate etc. 
derivatives: arjaka -arjya C. arjana E.+ arjanīya C. -arjayitṛ C. ṛjipyá RV. ṛjíśvan RV. ṛjīpín RV. ṛjīṣá RV. ṛjūnas RV. -ṛṅga RV. ṛjīyas V. ṛjú V.+ ráji RV. rájiṣṭha RV.B. rajīyas JB. rāji AV.+ 
It seems impossible to divide these forms (generally distributed to two different roots) from one another. The root has three well-marked stages of develoment: ṛj or ṛñj in Rv., arj in Brah., and arjaya in the later languge. Compare also √rāj, probably a derivative from it. With it is related, further, the anomalously formed stem irajya (irajyáti -te etc. RV., and irajyú RV.), 'direct, rule'.
